originalSource.fullRelevantText:
\subsection{A common completion kernel and its local remainders}

For a fixed $a>0$ let $I$ be either $(-a,a)$, $(-\infty,a)$, or
$(-a,\infty)$. For interior endpoints $y,z$ and $T>0$, define
\begin{equation}\label{cn:kerneldef}
 f^I_a(y,T;z)=\frac{k_T^I(y,z)}{\phi_T(z-y)},\qquad
 \phi_T(d)=(2\pi T)^{-1/2}e^{-d^2/(2T)}.
\end{equation}
This is the strict Brownian-bridge survival probability. We suppress $a,I$
when fixed. Its extension is zero if either endpoint is on or outside
the monitored walls. At a reachable zero-energy future its two endpoints
coincide; its value is one if that endpoint is interior. For terminal
envelopes only, a zero-variance bridge with different endpoints means
their deterministic linear interpolation. For $a=0$ all completions
are assigned zero.

Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of monitored wall signs: $\{+1,-1\}$ for
the interval, $\{+1\}$ for the upper half-line, and $\{-1\}$ for the
lower half-line. Write
\[
 d=z-y,\quad D=1+|d|/\sqrt T,\quad
 u_\eta=a-\eta y,\quad v_\eta=a-\eta z,
\]
\begin{equation}\label{cn:profiles}
 P(y,T;z)=\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal S}e^{-u_\eta v_\eta/T},
 \qquad
 P_b(y,T;z)=\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal S}
 e^{-(u_\eta-|b|)_+v_\eta/T}.
\end{equation}
In particular every such profile is at most two. Differentiation always
holds the walls and terminal endpoint fixed.

\begin{lemma}[Derivative and Taylor bounds]\label{cn:kernel}
For fixed nonnegative integers $j,l$, in particular for $j+l\le3$,
\begin{equation}\label{cn:derivative}
 |\partial_y^j\partial_T^l(f-1)|
 \le C_{j,l}T^{-j/2-l}D^jP(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
The same one-sided estimates hold at a wall. The quotient satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{cn:PDE}
 f_T=\tfrac12f_{yy}+(d/T)f_y.
\end{equation}
For $b^2\le T$, define the compensated remainder at an actual reveal by
\begin{equation}\label{cn:remainder}
 \mathfrak r_b=f_{\mathrm{ext}}(y+b,T-b^2;z)-f(y,T;z)
                 -(b-b^2d/T)f_y(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
If $b^2\le T/2$ and the new spatial point is in the closed domain,
\begin{equation}\label{cn:smallTaylor}
 |\mathfrak r_b|
 \le C|b|^3T^{-3/2}D^3P_b(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For a half-line, $f=1-e^{-2u_\eta v_\eta/T}$ by reflection. For
$\eta=+1$, put $C=2(a-y)(a-z)$; the reflected case is identical.
The exponent is affine in $y$, and
$|C_y|\le2|d|+\sqrt{2C}$. Repeated differentiation gives a polynomial
in $C/T$, times $C_y^jT^{-j-l}e^{-C/T}$. Absorbing the polynomial
and the powers of $\sqrt{C/T}$ into half the exponential proves
\eqref{cn:derivative}, with no lower bound on either endpoint.

For the interval, the image expansion divided by the free density is
\begin{align*}
 f&=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(e^{-A_m/T}-e^{-B_m/T}),\\
 A_m&=8m^2a^2+4ma d,\qquad
 B_m=2(y+(2m+1)a)(z+(2m+1)a).
\end{align*}
Here $A_0=0$ supplies the constant one; every other exponent is
nonnegative and affine in $y$. Each such exponent $C$ satisfies
$|C_y|\le2|d|+\sqrt{2C}$: for $A_m$ use
$A_m=(A_{m,y}-d)^2/2-d^2/2$, and for $B_m$ use that its two factors
have the same sign and differ by $d$. Thus a differentiated image term
is bounded by
\[
 C_{j,l}T^{-j/2-l}D^j e^{-C/(2T)}.
\]
When $T\le a^2$, set $B_0=2u_-v_-$ and $B_{-1}=2u_+v_+$.
For $m\ge1$,
\[
 B_m\ge B_0+8m^2a^2,\qquad
 A_m\ge B_0+8m(m-1)a^2.
\]
The second inequality follows from
$A_1-B_0=2(a-y)(3a+z)\ge0$ and $d\ge-2a$.
The negative side similarly has
$A_{-m}\ge B_{-1}+8m(m-1)a^2$, using
$A_{-1}-B_{-1}=2(a+y)(3a-z)\ge0$, and the analogous square tail
for the remaining $B$ terms. Their Gaussian series is bounded by a
constant times $P$. This proves \eqref{cn:derivative} in this range.

If $T\ge a^2$, the sine expansion of the killed heat kernel yields
\[
 |\partial_y^j\partial_T^l k_T^I|
 \le C_{j,l}T^{-(j+2l+1)/2}.
\]
For example, after taking absolute values its series is bounded by
$Ca^{-j-2l-1}\sum_{m\ge1}m^{j+2l}e^{-c m^2T/a^2}$;
the exponential dominates the required power for $T/a^2\ge1$.
Since $|d|/\sqrt T\le2$, derivatives of the reciprocal free density
have the corresponding bounds
$CT^{(1-j-2l)/2}$. Leibniz's rule bounds every positive-order
derivative of $f$ by $CT^{-j/2-l}$. For order zero use
$|f-1|\le1$. Finally $u_\eta v_\eta\le4a^2\le4T$, so
$P\ge2e^{-4}$. This proves the desired profile estimate also here.
The normally convergent positive-time expansions justify all
differentiations and one-sided traces. Dividing the heat equation for
$k$ by the free heat equation gives \eqref{cn:PDE}.

For \eqref{cn:smallTaylor}, apply second-order Taylor expansion along
$(y+sb,T-sb^2)$, $0\le s\le1$. Its variance time is in $[T/2,T]$,
its drift factor is at most $CD$, and its profile is at most $P_b$.
The leading terms are
\[
 b f_y-b^2 f_T+\tfrac12b^2f_{yy}
 =(b-b^2d/T)f_y.
\]
The other second-order terms are $-b^3f_{yT}+b^4f_{TT}/2$.
Each third-order directional term has normalized power
$(|b|/\sqrt T)^{j+2l}D^j$ with $j+l=3$. Since
$|b|/\sqrt T\le1$ and $j+2l\ge3$, all these terms are at most
$C|b|^3T^{-3/2}D^3P_b$. A point on the wall uses the smooth
one-sided zero trace.

\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A projection pays its own negative overshoot]\label{cn:projection}
Suppose $y,z\in I$ and $y+b$ hits or crosses a monitored wall with
sign $\eta=\operatorname{sign}(b)$, where $b^2\le T/2$. Put
\[
 B=|b|,\quad u=a-\eta y\in(0,B],\quad p=\eta u,\quad
 \delta=B-u,\quad c=1-\eta(B+u)d/T.
\]
Then, for the interval and either half-line,
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak r_b&=\mathfrak r_p+O_b,
 &O_b&=-\eta\delta c f_y,\qquad0\le c\le2D,
                                                        \label{cn:projectionid}\\
 |\mathfrak r_p|+(O_b)_-
 &\le CuB^2T^{-3/2}D^3
 \le CB^3T^{-3/2}D^3.                                  \label{cn:projectbound}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Both the crossing and its projection have zero completion, so
subtraction in \eqref{cn:remainder} proves the identity. Since
$\eta d<u$, one has
$c\ge1-2b^2/T\ge0$ and
$c\le1+2(B/\sqrt T)(D-1)\le2D$.
The projected segment has time at least $T/2$; thus
\eqref{cn:smallTaylor}, with $|p|=u$ and $P_p\le2$, gives
$|\mathfrak r_p|\le Cu^3T^{-3/2}D^3$.

Set $A=1-\eta ud/T\ge1-u^2/T\ge1/2$. Nonnegativity of $f$ and the exact identity
$\mathfrak r_p=-f-\eta uAf_y$ imply
$uA(\eta f_y)_+\le|\mathfrak r_p|$.
The identity $((B+u)/u)A-c=B/u$ gives $c/A\le(B+u)/u$, so
\[
 |\mathfrak r_p|+(O_b)_-
 \le\left(1+\frac{\delta(B+u)}{u^2}\right)|\mathfrak r_p|
 \le C\{u^3+\delta u(B+u)\}T^{-3/2}D^3
 =CuB^2T^{-3/2}D^3.
\]
The projected displacement need not be a remaining label. Equality
hits have $\delta=0$; the projected endpoint uses the one-sided wall trace.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One local Gaussian wall envelope]\label{cn:localprofile}
At any actual reveal state with $a,T>0$, $y,z\in I$ and $b^2\le T$,
let $\ell_b^I$ retain $\mathfrak r_b$ except at a small-energy crossing,
where it retains $\mathfrak r_p$. For each monitored wall put
\[
 w_\eta=a-\eta y,\quad M_\eta=|b|+(\eta d)_+,\quad
 \Pi=\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal S}e^{-((w_\eta-M_\eta)_+)^2/T},
 \qquad q=|b|/\sqrt T.
\]
Then, with the second term present only for an interval,
\begin{equation}\label{cn:localprofilebound}
 |\ell_b^I|+1_{\{\text{small-energy crossing}\}}(O_b)_-
 \le Cq^3D^3\Pi.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a small interior step use \eqref{cn:smallTaylor} and the wallwise
inequality
$(w_\eta-|b|)_+(w_\eta-\eta d)
\ge((w_\eta-M_\eta)_+)^2$, which gives $P_b\le\Pi$.
For a large interior step, $|f'-f|\le(1-f)+(1-f')$; each reflection
deficit is bounded by the sum of $e^{-2uv/T'}$ over monitored walls.
If $w_\eta>M_\eta$, all their endpoint distances from that wall
are at least $w_\eta-M_\eta$, and the future variance is at most $T$;
otherwise that wall's summand of $\Pi$ is one. Thus the deficits
cost $C\Pi$. By \eqref{cn:derivative}, the compensation is at most
$C(q+q^2|d|/\sqrt T)DP\le CqD^2\Pi$.
Here $q\le1$, and $q>1/\sqrt2$ lets $q^3$ pay both one and $q$.
At any crossing its crossed wall has $0<w_\eta\le|b|\le M_\eta$,
so $\Pi\ge1$: use \eqref{cn:projectbound} for a small crossing. At a large crossing its future completion is
zero, so $|f'-f|\le1$; the same compensation bound proves the claim.
Equality hits are crossings, and a reachable zero-time interior future
has deficit zero. No separated positive overshoot is included.
\end{proof}
